status: development-only replay smoke on an already-open PhysTwin-22 case
claim_boundary: This run may establish that an object-disjoint MatPhys spring field can be replayed through the official PhysTwin Warp simulator and consumed by the guarded Bayesian-PhysTwin backend. The case and its future were opened previously, so this run cannot establish independent transfer, calibration, or state of the art.

implementation.required_feature: paired factual-action and frame-zero-held-controller physical archive export

backends.incumbent: released PhysTwin checkpoint replayed by official PhysTwin Warp
backends.candidate: object-disjoint MatPhys spring_Y at strength 1.0 replayed by the same official PhysTwin Warp simulator
backends.identity_control: the incumbent replay exported through the same paired-action archive path

case.why_selected: The previously frozen object-disjoint family selector chose the nonzero alpha_1000 arm using only the declared prefix validation interval, and all required public artifacts are durably available.

execution.zero_action_semantics: hold every controller point at its frame-zero position while preserving gravity, support, collision, and the selected material field
execution.observation_semantics: hard-valid tracks only; cues do not depend on the PhysTwin state residual

gate.score: equal mean of candidate-to-incumbent validation CD and track ratios

advancement_rule: A successful replay only justifies freezing a genuinely fresh public-object source protocol. A larger claim additionally requires object-disjoint transfer, calibration, late-horizon, and worst-case-regression gates on that fresh panel.
forbidden: opening or scoring frames at or after frame 40 during this replay smoke
using future observations to alter the MatPhys spring field or proposal strength
changing the frozen Deform360 v6.1 candidate or scorer
using held-v8 runtime, target, query, score, barrier, or outcome artifacts
calling this already-open development case an independent confirmation or state-of-the-art result
